title: Thermal field

reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: One wrapped field read through a cyclic thermal colormap, cut by a cell grid that shifts, fans and flares it, with a colorbar that is its true scale.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 768 × 1408 and every length scales with the canvas

temp.does: Adds a constant to the whole field, which turns every color one step along the loop.

warm.does: The level the warm plateau holds: 0.43 is the measured orange 250 99 26; 0.5 is yellow.

span.does: Height of the three free domes that bend the field between the plateau and the pool, 0.25 to 0.55 turn each at 1.

tilt.does: A plain slope across the sheet, left to right, under the domes.

seed.does: Re-rolls the grid, the domes, the cell shifts and the hot spots.

cols.does: Columns across the sheet. Measured 63 to 76 px on 768: about 11.5.

rowH.does: Row height at the top. Measured 101 to 119 px in the upper two thirds.

shrink.does: How much the rows shrink toward the foot. Measured 112 px rows falling to 58 to 68 px in the bottom fifth.

lineW.does: Width of the cell lines. Measured 2 px.

lineDark.does: How far a line multiplies the field down. Measured 116 5 14 on a line over 245 75 50, and 94 55 0 over 247 185 12.

merge.does: Share of vertical segments left out, which merges two cells into one wide one.

jog.does: Share of horizontal segments shifted 3 to 6 px off their row line; a third of those also double, as at y 503 and 509 in the source.

cellNoise.does: A small random offset in every cell, so most cell edges carry a faint step in color, as most of the source's do.

shifts.does: Share of cells whose whole field is offset, which leaves a step in color along their edges.

shiftAmt.does: Largest offset a shifted cell takes.

fans.does: Cells whose field turns around one of their corners, 0.45 to 0.85 turn across the cell's quarter circle and fading over 1.8 times the cell's short side, so the colors meet at the corner like a pinwheel and stop at the cell's edges.

flares.does: Share of cells with a bright ridge hugging one edge, like the yellow along x 200 in the source.

spots.does: Clusters of small domes near grid crossings whose value climbs through whole turns, so each reads as rings of every color.

jet.does: A narrow ridge thrown from each cluster along its grid line that pulls the field toward yellow (0.5 to 0.56 turn) by the shortest way round the loop: the yellow column under the source's lower left cluster.

dither.does: σ of the grain added to the value before the colormap. The speckle lands where the map runs fast: high-pass σ 3.8 in the magenta band, 0.8 in the orange, 0.2 in the navy.

grain.does: Luminance grain screened over everything by the same field.

grainSize.does: Softening of the grain field. Measured lag-1 correlation 0.3 to 0.5.

phase.does: Position along the loop. Adds one turn to the field over the loop, so every color walks once around the map, the marker walks the colorbar and the grain boils.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Field
techniques.implementation: Warm plateau: the field held at 0.43 turn, orange 250 99 26, flat across several cells.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Flank: from orange down through red and magenta to violet; the dither speckle is densest here, σ 3.8.

techniques.name: Grid
techniques.implementation: Grid crossing: two 2 px lines that multiply the field to about 0.45 of its value.

techniques.name: Cells
techniques.implementation: Cell step: one cell offset by up to 0.09 turn, so its edges show a hard change of color.

techniques.name: Spot
techniques.implementation: Hot spot: small domes that climb whole turns, so each reads as rings of every color.

techniques.name: Foot
techniques.implementation: Colorbar: the same lookup drawn over one turn, 0 to 1, so it is the true scale of the field above.

pass_order: grid: columns 0.9 to 1.1 of W / 11.5 wide, rows 112 px that shrink toward the foot; vertical segments dropped to merge cells, horizontal segments jogged 3 to 6 px and some doubled
field in turns: offset plus a tilt, three free domes, then two flat-topped mixes that pull the warm plateau to orange one turn up and the cold pool to navy at the turn
cells: a small step in every cell, larger shifts in a few, fans that turn the field around one corner inside the cell, flares along one edge
hot spots: clusters of 2 to 4 small domes that climb whole turns, each throwing a jet along its grid line that pulls the field toward yellow
one grain field dithers the value before the cyclic colormap and screens the tones
lines: the field multiplied down along every cell edge, 2 px, anti-aliased
foot: caption, a colorbar drawn from the same lookup over one turn, its axis, end ticks, a marker at the phase, tick labels 0 to 1 and the x positions of three grid lines

colormap.method: k-means (28) on every other pixel of the field above the foot, dark line mixes dropped, centers ordered by hue; stop positions by Oklab arc length; the colors close on navy 3 7 109, so the map is a loop
colormap.order: navy, violet 61 25 148, magenta 179 2 151, red 245 4 71, orange 250 99 26, yellow 248 186 10, olive 175 179 73, green 67 160 118, teal 4 145 148, blue 3 87 165, deep blue 6 22 131, navy

grid.method: rows and columns where a pixel is 12 L darker than both neighbors 3 px away, share above 0.25
grid.row_px: 101 to 119 in the upper two thirds, 58 to 68 in the bottom fifth
grid.jogs: 503 and 509 at one crossing, 823 and 829 at another

line.method: row and column profiles across the lines

grain_hp_sigma.method: L minus a 2 px gaussian over 60 to 120 px patches; the spread follows how fast the map runs

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Thermal loop palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The field is generated, so the region patches sit on the same material in the render, placed with search.py within the matching region: the warm plateau, the magenta flank, the cold pool. The caption is set to the source's wording for the foot patch; the render's colorbar is the true scale of its field, which the source's is not.

limits: Bench mean 0.910, lowest 0.61 (the foot's warm bar ink, below). The furthest of the four from 0.98. The field is generated, and the source's is a single drawn composition: an orange column on the left third, a magenta diagonal, a blue right side, a navy foot. The whole-field histogram and ink shares score 0.82 to 0.97 because the render's warm plateau, flank and pool fall in different places and proportions; the three region patches were placed with search.py inside the matching region and still score 0.71 to 0.95 on histogram and contrast.

The grid-crossing spectrum scores 0.68 and the cold-corner structure 0.84: the source's lines fade into its navy and its corner is nearly noiseless, σ 0.2, while the render's lines stay at a constant depth and its cell steps add edges.

The foot's warm bar ink scores 0.63 by design: the source's colorbar is a row of out-of-order blocks that does not match its field; the render's bar is the true scale of its own field over one turn, so its warm part is the narrow orange-to-yellow run of the loop.
The source is a JPEG with soft streaks around its crossings that the render does not model.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
